label: PF Backlog 505
title: Strict id allocation: PF_ID_ALLOC=strict (default) - require the git-CAS authority, fail closed, never self-reserve
body:
## Problem / why
The allocator's soft mode falls back to a LOCAL block when the shared git-CAS authority is unavailable, which can
re-collide across stale/offline sessions.

## Goal & value
A STRICT mode: allocation must succeed via the shared git authority; otherwise FAIL CLOSED (raise) - never
self-reserve. Default to strict (GitHub is assumed always available). Ops can set PF_ID_ALLOC=on (soft) for
environments without push access.

## Acceptance criteria
- PF_ID_ALLOC=strict (default): _mint requires the git-CAS; on failure it raises (no API/local fallback).
- _next_id does NOT swallow the strict error (propagates -> item creation fails closed).
- PF_ID_ALLOC=on keeps the soft fallback; =off disables the allocator.
- Tests run with PF_ID_ALLOC=on (isolated) so they do not require the remote.

## In scope
strict mode + env-flags declaration + non-swallowing _next_id.

## Out of scope
changing the CAS/counter mechanism.

## Verification
test: strict raises when the remote CAS is unavailable; a cache-bypassing strict test uses a temp remote.

brief.problem: the allocator soft-falls back to a local block when the shared authority is unreachable, which can re-collide
brief.what_adds: DEFAULT strict: allocation requires the shared git-CAS authority and fails closed; soft is an opt-in toggle (PF_ID_ALLOC=on)
brief.why: GitHub is always available, so strict gives a no-collision guarantee by default

_next_id propagates the strict error (no max+1 fallback)

approach: mode() from env_flags (default strict); _mint raises in strict when CAS fails; _next_id re-raises in strict
